newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch sugar output near one mln T -Suiker Unie.
newsitem.headline: Dutch sugar output near one mln T -Suiker Unie.

text.p: Total Dutch beet sugar output in the 1996/1997 season is forecast to be at or just above one million tonnes, the country's leading grower said on Thursday.
Dutch production in the 1995/96 season was 1.074 million tonnes and 1.051 million in 1994/95.
Alfons Calon, agricultural affairs director at Suiker Unie, told Reuters rainfall at the end of August this year had compensated for a dry summer and had improved the potential of the Dutch crop.

"We were very happy that the rain came, the leaf on the crop looks very healthy but a lot depends on what weather we get in the coming few days," he told Reuters. "We should get a total Dutch crop of around a million tonnes, maybe just over."
Suiker Unie produces around 65 percent of Dutch sugar beet.
For the Suiker Unie crop alone, Calon estimated production this season at 650,000 tonnes with a root yield at 59 tonnes per hectare and a sugar content of 16 percent.
He said this was slightly higher than the recent forecasts on the whole crop from the Dutch Institute for Sugar Research (IRS), which put beet weight at 56.0 tonnes per hectare.
"We normally have a higher yield than the whole crop and thus more than the forecast from IRS," he said.
He said farmers would be looking for dry and sunny weather in the next few weeks. Depending on weather conditions, sugar content could rise to 16.2 percent or drop to 15.8.
"We are looking for sunny weather but also clear with cold nights -- that cuts the respiration of the plants and gives the best sugar building conditions," he said.
"If we get a lot of cold nights then the content could get up to 16.1 or 16.2 percent but it's a little early to tell."
